summary: Household: Texas, two adults (married) and two children, the youngest is 3. Household earned income about $21,400/yr, no Social Security or other income reported, rent about $450-700/mo, modest savings, no pregnancy, no disability or senior member, and someone has employer health insurance. Recommended: SNAP (income well under the gross limit for 4; Texas has no effective asset test in practice), WIC (child under 5, income under 185% FPL), Medicaid for the children (Texas adult Medicaid is very limited, but children qualify at this income), EITC (full or near-full credit with two children at this income), refundable child tax credit (about $2,800 refundable portion at this earnings level), and free school meals (income below the free-meal threshold for 4). Not recommended: TANF (Texas limits are far below this income), SSI (no disabled or aged member), CHIP (children's income band falls under Medicaid), and ACA premium tax credit (employer coverage is available). Caveat: ages of both children were not confirmed; the CTC assumes both are under 17.
